annotation.summary_en: A man struggling with alcoholism seeks advice from a priest in a park, but finds a clever excuse not to pour out his vodka.
annotation.summary_detailed_en: The sketch is set in an autumn park covered in fallen leaves, where a man dressed as a medieval Armenian monk-scribe, wearing a tall pointed hood and holding a manuscript, is approached by a man in an olive beanie and tan coat. The drunkard greets the priest and explains his problem: he cannot stop drinking and needs help. The priest advises him that he must first help himself before seeking divine intervention, instructing the man to go to a nearby tree and pour out his bottle of vodka. The man hesitates, explaining that he cannot empty the bottle because he shares it with a friend; they are partners in the drink. When the priest suggests he should simply pour out his own half, the man delivers the punchline: he cannot do that either, because his half is the one at the bottom of the bottle. The scene uses a shot-reverse-shot technique among the bare trees to highlight the absurdity of the man's logic for keeping his alcohol.
